title: Pizza with extra meat, thick crust

content.title: About
content.content: Pizza with extra meat and a thick crust is a classic Italian pizza made on a dough with a higher yeast content, giving the crust a fluffy and crunchy texture. It is topped with a generous layer of tomato sauce, mozzarella cheese, and a variety of meat ingredients such as ham, sausage, bacon, and beef.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: A thick crust requires a longer baking time, which intensifies the dough’s aroma.
Extra meat raises the calorie count but also adds protein and iron.
Traditionally a meat‑topped pizza is called “meat‑lover’s”, but regional variations add their own spices and sauces.
Dough for a thick crust is often mixed with a small amount of olive oil, making it more elastic.
Some pizzerias use a special baking stone to achieve the perfect crunch.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: The meat provides a complete source of protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Iron source
items.content: Red meat is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Mozzarella supplies calcium that supports bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and the yeast in the dough deliver B1, B2, B6, and B12 vitamins important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Lipids for energy
items.content: Fats from meat and cheese provide a sustained energy source.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: The abundance of meat and cheese makes the pizza calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Meat products and cheese can contain saturated fats, which may affect cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Sausages and ham are often salty, which can be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to dairy proteins should choose alternative cheeses or omit them entirely.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pizza hot, sliced into individual portions. Fresh vegetables such as tomatoes or arugula can be added after baking for a flavor balance. Optionally sprinkle a little Parmesan or drizzle with olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore crust crispness. The pizza can be frozen for up to 2 months if wrapped tightly in plastic film and foil.
